# Mesfin Genie

::: {.standfirst}
Senior Lecturer in Health Economics, Newcastle Business School, University of Newcastle
:::

I measure what people are willing to give up. Patients trade waiting time against
cost, side effects against survival, privacy against convenience; governments make
the same trades on their behalf and rarely say so out loud. My work puts numbers on
those trades using discrete choice experiments, and then asks a harder question:
whether the numbers mean what we think they mean when a person has only skimmed
half the information in front of them. That second question is why I run eye
trackers alongside surveys.

Most of it ends up somewhere concrete. Vaccine mandate preferences became a tool
policymakers can open in a browser. A World Bank choice experiment became a costing
model for scaling up field-epidemiology training. I am at Newcastle after a PhD at
Ca' Foscari Venice and posts at Aberdeen, Auburn and Duke.

[Papers](/publications/), [tools](/tools/), [CV](/cv/), or write to me at
[mesfin.genie@newcastle.edu.au](mailto:mesfin.genie@newcastle.edu.au).

:::

## Answer three questions and I will price your patience

```{=html}
<div class="ct" id="choice-task">
  <div class="ct-frame">

    <div id="ct-ask">
      <p class="ct-q">Question <span id="ct-n">1</span> of 3</p>
      <p class="ct-stem">You need to see a specialist. Two clinics can take you, and they are alike in every way except these two. Which do you book?</p>

      <div class="ct-grid">
        <div class="ct-cell ct-head"><span class="visually-hidden">Attribute</span></div>
        <div class="ct-cell ct-head">Clinic A</div>
        <div class="ct-cell ct-head">Clinic B</div>

        <div class="ct-cell ct-attr">Wait for an appointment</div>
        <div class="ct-cell ct-val">2 weeks</div>
        <div class="ct-cell ct-val">6 weeks</div>

        <div class="ct-cell ct-attr">Cost to you</div>
        <div class="ct-cell ct-val" id="ct-bid">$80</div>
        <div class="ct-cell ct-val">No cost</div>
      </div>

      <div class="ct-actions">
        <span></span>
        <button type="button" class="ct-pick" data-pick="A">Book Clinic A</button>
        <button type="button" class="ct-pick" data-pick="B">Book Clinic B</button>
      </div>

      <div class="ct-dots" aria-hidden="true">
        <span class="ct-dot"></span>
        <span class="ct-dot"></span>
        <span class="ct-dot"></span>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div id="ct-out" class="ct-result" tabindex="-1" aria-live="polite">
      <p class="ct-q">What your three answers imply</p>
      <p class="ct-answer" id="ct-answer"></p>

      <div class="ct-figure">
        <div class="ct-bar"><div class="ct-band" id="ct-band"></div></div>
        <div class="ct-scale"><span>$0</span><span>$150</span><span>$300 or more</span></div>
      </div>

      <p class="note">Each question raised or lowered the price depending on the answer before it, so three choices bracket the point where you switch. That is the whole logic of stated-preference work, run on one person. A real discrete choice experiment does it across hundreds of respondents and six or seven attributes at once, and estimates the switching point instead of bracketing it, which is what makes the number transferable to someone other than you.</p>

      <button type="button" class="ct-restart" id="ct-restart">Start again</button>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<p class="note" style="margin-top:1rem;">The tools under [Tools](/tools/) run the same machinery on estimated coefficients rather than on your three answers.</p>
```

```{=html}
<li class="rec">
  <div class="rec-year">2026</div>
  <div class="rec-body">
    <p class="rec-title">Fit for purpose? Discrete choice experiment designs for changing health technologies</p>
    <p class="rec-venue">Social Science &amp; Medicine</p>
    <p class="rec-finding">A choice experiment describes a technology as it stood when the design was written. When the technology moves, the design can quietly stop measuring the thing it was built to measure. This sets out when that happens and what to do about it.</p>
  </div>
</li>
```

## Students and teaching

I teach behavioural economics and health economics at Newcastle, and supervise
students working on choice experiments, eye tracking and clinical outcomes
measurement. If you are thinking about a PhD or a Master's project, read
[what to send me](/supervision/) before writing; it will save us both a round of
email. Course details are under [teaching](/teaching/).
